title: Measuring distance with a map scale
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank's map conventions card only says the scale links map distance to ground distance as one of six map parts, while the new point teaches the skill of converting a measured distance using a line or ratio scale, and the scale-of-study card is about geographic extent rather than map scale.

draft.title: Measuring distance with a map scale
card: A map scale links a distance on the map to the real distance on the ground. It lets you work out how far apart two places really are.
a bar marked in kilometres or metres. Measure the map distance with a ruler, then lay it along the bar to read the real distance.
written like 1:50 000. One unit on the map stands for 50 000 of the same unit on the ground. So 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm, which is 500 m.
To use a ratio scale, measure the map distance, multiply it by the second number, then change the units. For example, 4 cm on a 1:50 000 map is 200 000 cm, which is 2 km.
draft.remember: Measure on the map, then use the scale to turn it into the real distance.

a.q: A map has a ratio scale of 1:25 000. What does 1 cm on the map stand for?
a.why: In a ratio scale, 1 unit on the map is 25 000 of the same unit on the ground, so 1 cm is 25 000 cm. The option with metres mixes up the units, because the units on both sides of the ratio are the same.
a.clue: Both sides of the ratio use the same unit.

b.q: Priya measures 6 cm between a campsite and a lookout on a map with a scale of 1:50 000. How far apart are they on the ground?
b.why: 6 cm × 50 000 = 300 000 cm, which is 3000 m or 3 km. The answer of 300 m comes from a slip when changing units, and 30 km is a slip in the other direction.
b.clue: Multiply by 50 000, then change centimetres to kilometres.
